_meta.purpose: External SWE-bench Verified baseline claims for models Drake is weighing for local (256GB-class hardware) runs, gathered so his own model-eval gauntlet results have something to sit next to. See README.md in this directory for the full caveat on why these numbers are directional-only against model-eval's own task results.
_meta.collected_by: research seats (per Drake handoff, seat: implementer, studio/baseline-data)
_meta.revised: 2026-08-24 per PR #2 review (pullrequestreview-5009501140): one misattributed record, two unsourced provenance claims, and several mechanical fixes -- see known_gaps below and the PR thread for the full rationale.
_meta.schema_notes: Fields added in the 2026-08-24 revision, used only where the source data requires them: independent_verified (bool/null) -- whether the independent figure's source was actually located at a URL, not just whether an evaluator name was recorded; approx_independent (string) -- used instead of a typed number when the source itself states the figure is approximate, so a parser can't read false precision; swe_bench_verified_vendor_scaffold / _alt / _alt_scaffold -- used only when a source reports more than one scaffold for the vendor figure, so the file records both instead of resolving to one cherry-picked number.
known_gaps: source_urls: populated on every record from the PR #2 review's verified table (2026-08-24) plus this seat's own WebFetch spot-checks. Four figures could not be located at any URL and are recorded as unverified rather than guessed or silently kept: GLM-4.6's Scale AI independent figure (68.2, independent_verified: false), Kimi K2.5's Fireworks independent figure (76.8, independent_verified: false), the DeepSeek '8% pass@1 leakage' contamination-audit claim (removed -- see the contamination_flag gap below), and gpt-oss-120b's community reproduction (~62, two conflicting unsourced harness numbers -- see approx_independent on that record).

fits_256gb is null except where Drake's handoff stated one explicitly (Kimi K2.5: false). quant_planned is null on every record, including Kimi K2.5 -- there is no exception for quant_planned. (A prior draft of this gap statement wrongly implied the Kimi K2.5 exception covered both fields.)

contamination_flag is null (unassessed) on every record. A prior draft set it true on the DeepSeek record, citing an '8% pass@1 leakage' audit that could not be located anywhere. NIST CAISI's own page attributes its lower scores to 'system prompt, scaffolding, and token budget differences,' not contamination. Null means unassessed -- not clean, and not accused either.

DeepSeek family naming: Drake's original handoff recorded benchmark values against the family name 'DeepSeek V4', which is ambiguous between two real, differently-sized models -- V4-Flash (291B) and V4-Pro (1.6T), per the vendor org page (huggingface.co/deepseek-ai), exposed as distinct API endpoints. Both numbers in this file's original single DeepSeek record (80.6 vendor, 74 NIST CAISI) belong to V4-Pro, not V4-Flash. The record has been renamed to DeepSeek V4-Pro and a separate, mostly-null DeepSeek V4-Flash record added rather than guessing Flash's numbers.

Unverified independent figures despite exact vendor agreement: GLM-4.6's Scale AI figure (68.2) and Kimi K2.5's Fireworks figure (76.8) both agree with their vendor figures to a tenth of a point, and neither could be located at a URL. On this benchmark, scaffold/prompt/token-budget differences normally produce a gap between vendor and independent figures (see the DeepSeek and Devstral records) -- exact agreement is the anomaly here, not confirmation. Both are independent_verified: false; do not treat them as corroboration until sourced.

Two more corrections applied in the 2026-08-24 revision: Qwen3-Coder-Next's vendor figure previously carried an invented 'best of 3 scaffolds' provenance story; the source reports two scaffolds side by side (SWE-Agent 70.6, OpenHands 71.3), both now recorded explicitly instead of implying a selection. gpt-oss-120b's community figure was previously recorded as the int 62, which falsely implied precision the source doesn't have; moved to a separate approx_independent string field, with swe_bench_verified_independent set to null.

models.notes: No independent SWE-bench Verified reproduction found as of the handoff date. Vendor-only figure -- treat as an upper bound.

Vendor figure (68.0) sourced from the GLM model card and docs.z.ai. The Scale AI SEAL leaderboard independent figure (68.2) is UNVERIFIED: the leaderboard (labs.scale.com/leaderboard/swe_bench_verified) is JS-rendered and no page surfaced 68.2 anywhere on two separate fetch attempts. Exact agreement with vendor to a tenth of a point is a reason for suspicion, not corroboration -- do not cite this figure until it is located at a URL.

Reattributed 2026-08-24: a prior draft of this file recorded these numbers under 'DeepSeek V4-Flash'. Both belong to V4-Pro. 'DeepSeek V4' is a family, not a model -- the vendor org page lists two separate lines, V4-Flash (291B) and V4-Pro (1.6T), exposed as distinct API endpoints (deepseek-v4-flash / deepseek-v4-pro). 80.6 is on the V4-Pro model card (column labelled 'DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max', a third variant name within the Pro line). 74 (reported by the source as an integer, not 74.0) is NIST CAISI's V4-Pro figure -- no CAISI figure for Flash exists. On the 6.6pp gap: NIST CAISI's own page attributes its lower scores to 'system prompt, scaffolding, and token budget differences' (500k weighted tokens), not contamination. No source was found for a held-out '8% pass@1 leakage' audit that a prior draft cited on this record -- contamination_flag is null (unassessed), not true. Do not re-add a leakage claim without a citable primary source (e.g. a yage.ai DeepSWE-style audit) at a URL; none was located in this pass.

Added 2026-08-24 as a separate record after finding 1 of the PR #2 review: the prior single 'DeepSeek V4-Flash' record actually carried V4-Pro's numbers (see the DeepSeek V4-Pro record). No SWE-bench Verified figure specific to V4-Flash (291B, per the vendor org page) was located in this pass -- recorded as null/unknown rather than guessed. 256GB-class local fit is a live open question for this variant in particular, since it is the smaller of the two V4 lines and the one plausibly in scope for local hardware.

Corrected 2026-08-24: a prior draft claimed this was a 'best of 3 scaffolds' optimistic-selection number. The technical report reports two scaffolds side by side -- SWE-Agent 70.6, OpenHands 71.3 -- which is ordinary practice for this benchmark, not selection among three. Both are now recorded explicitly (see swe_bench_verified_vendor_alt) instead of implying a cherry-picked single figure.

Vendor figure (76.8) sourced from the Kimi K2.5 model card. The Fireworks independent figure, also 76.8, is UNVERIFIED -- no Fireworks blog post or page matching this figure was located (blog archive checked; only Kimi K3 posts surfaced as of this pass). Exact agreement to the decimal with vendor is a reason for suspicion, not confirmation -- do not cite this figure until it is located at a URL. Explicitly flagged by Drake as NOT fitting a 256GB host -- out of scope for the local-model runs this baseline is meant to support unless that changes.

Largest vendor/independent gap in this set: 21.8pp (72.2 vendor vs 50.4 vals.ai). vals.ai figure verified at snippet level (full page not scraped). No contamination audit cited either way -- the gap alone is reason to weight the vals.ai figure over the vendor figure until more is known.
